messages:
Ana: Heads-up — saw a burst of 413s from tenant t-89 when they posted a single request with ~50 mixed-dim vectors (~18MB). Ingress splitter rejected the whole payload. :facepalm:
Jon: Which path emitted the 413? gateway or splitter? Logs?
Ana: gateway returned 413, splitter log shows 'payload too large' and then a single rejected batch entry. No fragmentation happened server-side.
Karen: Current contract is naive: max_bytes_per_request = 10MB, max_vectors=2048. We should clarify semantics for mixed-dim arrays - do we count by total bytes or by per-vector dim?
Liam: Count by serialized payload bytes makes the most sense for quotas, but batching/route behavior matters more for perf. If we split a request into N subrequests we risk scattering to different shard pools -> KV cache misses and higher tail latency.
Ana: For Dedicated tenants that's unacceptable. Need a tenant-affine fragmentation so subchunks stay on same capacity pool.
Jon: Right. Two orthogonal problems: (1) quota/validation semantics (2) server-side fragmentation + routing affinity.
Karen: Proposal A: immediate UX/contract change — preflight endpoint that returns exact split plan (list of fragment sizes) and a client SDK helper to split. Friendly 413 with link to SDK and docs. Low-risk rollout.
Liam: Proposal B: server-side fragmentation that preserves ordering and routes all fragments with a hint header `X-Embed-Fragment-Group` so router pins to same tenant pool. More op risk but UX is better for users.
Ana: For some customers ordering matters (they rely on stable id->vector mapping). Any fragmentation must include sequence ids and final "complete" marker.
Jon: Implementation sketch for B:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Headers: X-Embed-Fragment-Group: <uuid>
Body: { vectors: [...], fragment_index: 0, fragments_total: 3 }
```
Router uses X-Embed-Fragment-Group to maintain tenant-affine routing for the life of the request.
Karen: Telemetry we need: `embed.fragmented_count`, `embed.fragment_size_histogram`, `embed.413_by_tenant`, and `embed.fragment_affinity_misses`. Expose per-route + per-tenant breakdown in console.
Liam: Also add `embed.kvcache_miss_rate` correlated with fragmentation to measure perf impact.
Ana: Rollout plan suggestion: implement server-side fragmentation behind an account flag (opt-in). Start with non-tenant-critical default: fragmented requests get routed to same pool but flagged in trace. After 2 weeks, evaluate perf and decide on opt-in->auto.
Jon: For quotas: keep quota enforcement on original request semantics (bytes + vectors) but downstream shards accept fragments if original would exceed limit. Need to ensure quota accounting is idempotent (don't double-charge).
Karen: Console UX: show a tiny badge in request inspector "fragmented" with link to timeline showing fragment sizes and latencies. Also a tenant-level toggle: "Allow server-side fragmentation (beta)".
Liam: Tests: need order-preservation unit/regression tests and an integration perf harness that sends mixed-dim large posts and measures tail lat.
Ana: Quick client-side mitigation — SDK emits warning when sending mixed dims >5MB: "Consider `client.batch_by_dim()` or enable server-side fragmentation in console."
devex-bot: Created issue INF-4321: router: tenant-affine fragmentation + telemetry (assigned Jon).
Jon: I'll prototype router change and header semantics this week. Karen — can you do the console mockups for the fragment inspector?
Karen: Yup, will sketch flows: opt-in toggle, badge, histogram, and a per-tenant fragmentation history table.
Liam: Note about autoscaling: if all fragments pin to same pool we may create hot tenants. Need soft cap and fallback to multi-pool routing with partial KV warming. Add `embed.fragment_fallback` metric.
Ana: Good call. Also need a graceful error message for clients that don't support fragmentation: include `supports_fragmentation: true|false` in SDK handshake.
Jon: Timeline: PR for router + telemetry by Fri, console mock by next Wed, canary opt-in next Tue, observe metrics for 2 weeks then decide.
Karen: I'll add a small explainer in the console 'Why do my requests fragment?' modal.
Ana: I'll add regression unit for ordering + an e2e that verifies no double billing.
Liam: +perf microbench. If we see >10% tail regression we revert.
Ana: Cool. For immediate mitigation I'm going to add clearer 413 payload message with suggested client code sample for splitting.
Jon: sample in docs we can add:
```
# python
from redwood_embed import split_by_bytes
chunks = split_by_bytes(vectors, max_bytes=8*1024*1024)
for c in chunks:
  client.embed.create(c)
```
Liam: OK. Anything else?
Karen: add UI telemetry checkbox for "notify me when a tenant’s requests are fragmented > X/day".
Ana: Thanks all. Follow-ups: Jon (router PR), Karen (console mocks), Liam (perf harness), Ana (SDK warning + docs), devex-bot created INF-4321.
Jon: sounds good. I'll drop progress updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
